Subject: Post-call: GDPR / DPA + SCC module selection (Acme Corp.)

Hi Samantha —

Great to meet you and Tom on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the procurement side: 

- Key ask from your side: standard DPA + confirmation of which SCC module applies for EU data transfers.
- What we heard: Acme will be acting as the Controller, Redwood as Processor (please confirm below if that aligns).
- Redwood action items: share our DPA template and SCC mapping recommendation; confirm SOC 2 availability and scope; provide DocuSign-ready DPA if acceptable.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Template_v2.pdf, SCC_Module_Matrix.xlsx (high-level mapping to module numbers + notes).

Proposed next steps: 
1) Please confirm Acme's role (Controller vs Processor) for the workloads discussed (expected: Controller).
2) Fill out the vendor security questionnaire we discussed (if helpful, you can share it and we’ll loop in Rishi to complete the technical sections).
3) If the DPA template looks standard to you, we can send a DocuSign copy for review and signature; typical timeline from signature to go-live is ~2 weeks for our standard config.

Happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up if that helps speed things along.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — good recap. Quick answers and requests: 

- Confirmed: Acme will be Controller for the customer data in this integration.
- We generally sign vendor DPAs and expect the vendor to adopt SCC Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor). Can you confirm Redwood recommends Module 2 as well?
- We need to validate SOC 2 Type II status and ask for a redacted report; also our procurement team wants to know whether Redwood will accept the Acme standard DPA redlines (we have a few commercial/legal asks).

I've attached our vendor security questionnaire (Acme_VSQ_2026.xlsx) — please have the security team complete the technical sections and return. If easier, we can provide a DocuSign URL for our DPA, otherwise we can review Redwood's template.

Can you also confirm whether you process any special categories of personal data and how subject rights requests are handled? This will help our privacy team align the DPA.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Director, Procurement | Acme Corp.
samantha.lee@acme-corp.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: GDPR / DPA + SCC module selection (Acme Corp.)

Thanks Samantha — and appreciate the VSQ. Quick answers while Rishi digs into the VSQ / SOC2 specifics: 

- SCC module: Yes — Module 2 (Controller → Processor) is the correct selection for the flow you described. In the SCC_Module_Matrix.xlsx attached earlier we highlight Module 2 and the standard addenda items we typically accept.
- DPA: Our standard DPA is attached (Redwood_DPA_Template_v2.pdf). We can sign either our DPA or review Acme's DPA redlines. For speed, we typically exchange via DocuSign; I attached a suggested DocuSign link for you to use if that helps: https://www.docusign.com/sign/acme-redwood-dpa-req
- Special categories: We do not expect to process special category personal data for the use cases discussed (no health or biometric data). If that changes, we'll surface it immediately in the DPA.
- Subject rights: We support standard subject access and deletion workflows; detailed instructions/procedures can be added as an appendix.

Rishi — can you pick up the VSQ (attached) and the request for a redacted SOC 2 Type II? If you can confirm the SOC 2 report availability and any relevant scope exclusions, that will help Acme procurement move forward.

Proposed timeline: if we get the completed VSQ and confirm SCC Module 2 / sign DPA, we can target contracting within ~10 business days.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Hi Samantha / Marissa — looping in Security & Legal to close out the remaining items. 

SOC 2 status: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit covering our inference platform and associated access controls (period: Jan 1 2025 - Dec 31 2025). We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; redacted copy: SOC2_TypeII_Redacted_2025.pdf.

Scope notes: the SOC 2 covers logical access, change management, incident response, and encryption-in-transit and at-rest. Our KMS is customer-key capable for Private deployments; hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys with standard rotation.

SCC / DPA: we confirm Module 2 (Controller → Processor) is appropriate for Acme's described flow and our legal team is prepared to review Acme redlines. For execution we can do either: exchange DocuSign of Redwood's template or review Acme's DocuSign packet. Legal contact: legal-contracts@redwood.ai (please include your legal contact and any required PO or reference number).

VSQ: we'll have security complete the technical sections in the attached VSQ and return by EOD Tue 16 Jun (aiming for faster if possible). If you want to expedite the SOC2 exchange, please send over an NDA and we’ll prioritize.

If helpful, Neha can set a 15-min legal handoff with Acme procurement to align on redlines and timeline.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
